### Video 1

**Season 11 Vanessa Guide with Volf | The Bazaar Vanessa Over-Explained** — Volf (2,080 followers) — 7,438 views — uploaded 2026-02-09 — 3,495 s (~58 min) — https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=893fsuBXR4w

**Authority signals:** Says he plays in "Bazaar League" and (jokingly) counts himself a pro for the thumbnail; calls weapons his real expertise and this aquatic/burn run a secondary line; the run ends as a 10-win "perfect victory", which he openly calls a high roll.

#### Core claims
- Early aquatics are strong right now because of cheap defence: Coral Armor (called slept-on), Seaweed, Sea Shell. With that much shield you do not need much offence early.
- Run burn plus poison together early; two damage types hedge against opposing counters.
- Day 1: do not take the econ option. He took a skill, then the Kina merchant, and bought Coral Armor, Yeti Crab and Volcanic Vents, then rolled (2 gold) for a small such as Lighter.
- Buy a Coral and sell it purely to add +10 to Coral Armor; buy Sea Shell for the same reason (it buffs Coral Armor) and it can also be played.
- Put burn buffs (Cinders from loot, Curio buffs) on the fast item (Lighter or Pop Snappers), not on Volcanic Vents: more applications, earlier high burn numbers, and those smalls stay on the board longer than Vents.
- Take loot-item nodes (e.g. Jungle Ruins) whenever playing burn, on any hero, because they can give Cinders (+burn).
- Health target on Vanessa and Stelle: about 200 bonus max health; taking silver chocolate twice gets there. Rest is fine before PvP but is "bait" before PvE.
- When non-weapons, prefer the "enchanted small" reward; enchanted non-weapon smalls are very strong. A skill roll (Pip (?)) has a higher ceiling for burn but worse misses.
- Hedge win conditions in the stash: he bought Iceberg before having Primordial (?) (the item he later calls "big squid"), then fully pivoted when Primordial and Incendiary Rounds both appeared.
- Steal a level with XP nodes: level 10 and level 13 are the big breakpoints, 12 matters less; once past the breakpoint, stop taking XP and take enchant/loot instead.
- Street Festival is "broken": it can hand you a game-winning enchanted item (Lux (?) there).

#### Notable details
- Burn timing trick: a cooldown buff taking Lighter from 3.0 s to 2.9 s lets the burn land just before the tick at 3.0 s, effectively stealing one tick.
- Vents fires at 7 s and 14 s; Lighter at 3/6/9/12. His count at 12 s: Pop Snappers 24 burn applied versus 18 from Vents.
- Heavy Lighter (slow enchant) plus Improvised Bludgeon (slow duration buff from Curio) plus a further slow buff ended as a 2.8 s cooldown, 5 s slow Lighter. Slow on a permanent board item also opens slow synergies.
- Shadowed Cloak next to Lighter keeps it hasted; he upgraded the Cloak because its upgrade is harder to find than burn-item upgrades, then cut it later.
- Banannibal (?) gives an overheal-to-haste skill; it combos with Ambergris or any heal enchant plus Holsters.
- Economy: Chum can always be bought and resold at cost and leaves a Piranha (counts as a "friend" for the tiny furry monster (?) event). Ambergris pays back on aquatic purchases, so buying Jellyfish, Salt Claw or Chum is roughly free. Lockbox costs 6, gains 3 value per win, so it sells for 7 after one win. A discounted merchant (Vulpak (?)) lets you farm Ambergris. Shovel "has to be kept". Docks-item node is a premium econ and XP source.
- Cove: buy at bronze always; at silver it cost all his gold, so he skipped.
- Kwixel (?): good small/medium pool but rolling costs 4 gold.
- Fight picks: prefers the Thief over Coconut Crab (lower ceiling, reliable gold); Product Demonstrator now gives decent gold; Suds (?) for gold and Dishwasher; Hakurvian (?) is easy despite "virus".
- Solar Farm with Rocket Boots becomes a 2 s item.
- Mid-game tempo pivot (around day 5): Arbalest with a board-wide haste enchant hit for about 700. It needs only one ammo; he sold a duplicate before taking Gunpowder so the Gunpowder went elsewhere.
- Final board logic: Primordial charges 2 s whenever you burn, poison or freeze; Dive Weights (multicast 4 from ammo, hastes, cuts cooldown of adjacent aquatics) sits next to Incendiary Rounds and Primordial; Lighter and Pop Snappers supply fast burn procs; a fiery enchant goes on Iceberg so each enemy item use gives two Primordial charges; arrange so the most crit lands on Primordial. Burning Rage (?) on a 4-multicast item added an estimated 800 damage.
- Oceanic Rush: keep only one or two aquatics so the haste is targeted (e.g. Clamera plus one other).
- Mal'fang (?) fire-skill merchant: good when you need more burn procs (to speed Zoarcid or feed Blaze Hell (?)); pool is wide. He dislikes the poison merchant on Vanessa.
- Gumballs: strictly correct to buy and sell one at a time.

#### Caveats or disagreements
- Repeatedly says "dealer's choice" on day-1 picks and on Lighter-versus-Vents buff placement.
- The burn half-tick claim is prefaced with "I believe".
- Primordial was nerfed this patch (scaling per trigger 20 instead of 25, he says); previously it one-shot more often. Toxic Flame is described as gutted.
- Admits the run was a high roll with easy opponents; unsure about Iceberg as plug-and-play, and still not a Salt Claw believer.

### Video 2

**Season 11 Vanessa Weapons Guide with Volf | The Bazaar Vanessa Over-Explained** — Volf (2,080 followers) — 3,649 views — uploaded 2026-02-10 — 3,497 s (~58 min) — https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=o4d_JSV9Id4

**Authority signals:** Claims weapons Vanessa (especially Shuriken) is the thing he knows best and is known for; says a previous attempt was discarded because it missed weapons; beats the Lich monster and wins the run, while repeatedly rating his luck (top 20-30%, later "top 3%").

#### Core claims
- Weapons want fast, scalable weapons: Katana, Fang, Narwhal, Shark Claws, Handaxe. His summary: collect many fast triggers, then multiply them (flat weapon damage, crit, more triggers), and once damage is enough, look for speed.
- A weapon-damage skill is mandatory; without one the build stalls. Take the weapon-skill reward over enchanted items every time. Best: Strength (?), Left/Right-Handed, Deadly Waters (?) (aquatic weapons; good with Narwhal and Shark Claws), Bloodhound (called the best weapon skill), Inexorable (?) for crit.
- Play full offence; max health is the defence. Extra shield items dilute damage scaling.
- Buy cheap weapons for health: each bought weapon gave him +20 max health (via a skill or event he took (?)), which he prices like silver chocolate (100 health for 5 gold, i.e. 1 gold per 20).
- Take every ammo source: Hoverbike (?) fight, Preening Duelist (?) (ammo skill, Pistol Sword), any Gunpowder node or loot node.
- Pistol Sword is the default end game and easiest to reach; Shuriken can solo carry; Blow Gun is a high-roll alternative that needs scaling, charge and crit; Powder Keg and Anchor are crit lines.
- With no direction and spare gold, keep rolling.
- Curio is close to mandatory for weapons with Katana: Shadowed Cloak on Katana "breaks the game", and cheap flat damage buffs are large on fast weapons.
- If you only need to survive the day (days 4-5), Jules' Cafe plus-damage nearly guarantees a win.

#### Notable details
- Day 1: Katana, Calico (?), Shark Claws, Narwhal bought in the first shop. Finn's Big Bite (?) regen (5 per second) is estimated at 50+ health per fight plus 15 base, and he credits it for beating a long fight. Kyver Drone: fielding no items guarantees the win, since its Stinger and Trained Spider (?) only scale off you.
- Calico at silver is a roughly 14 s "clock": other weapons build its crit, then it hits after two Shark Claws procs (he saw 105-150). Late, moving Calico to the right slot for Right-Handed made it a temporary carry.
- Pet Rock: he treats board-wide crit as about a 1.15x damage multiplier; another crit option as 1.08x. Crow's Nest is 40% crit across the board.
- "Eight seconds and you're dead" theory: Shark Claws fires at 6 s, then a 5-multicast Shuriken kills by 8 s.
- Dive Weights is the combo engine: each ammo is a multicast (6-7 in this run), each cast hastes a weapon, and it loses only one ammo per use (7 procs, then 6, then 5). Holsters and Rocket Boots belong on it; he held Rocket Boots for most of the game for this. Slow-enchanted Dive Weights pairs with Kusarigama.
- Rocket Boots: haste buffs are hard to find; damage and slow buffs are common (Curio has two slow buffs).
- Gold: an event paying +2 gold per weapon would have been 16. Hellbilly (?) is taken for high average gold, a ticket and Left-Handed; Treasure Turtle for most gold.
- A free +5 damage to all weapons is "half a Strength"; the 15-gold version is only for rich, settled boards.
- Zoarcid plus Lighter/Pop Snappers/Vents fits weapons too; Pop Snappers also hedges Pistol Sword.
- Figurehead: silver good days 2-4, gold days 4-8, diamond days 10-13. Swash Buckle gives crit and damage per trigger. Captain's Quarters can replace Shark Claws (hastes Dive Weights, board buff, reload).
- Late game: silver Shark Claws as the only damage buff on day 8 is a warning sign. He bought Kusarigama, then Blow Gun, lost one fight narrowly, then found Pistol Sword: about 210-232 damage per ammo use, times seven Dive Weights casts. Kusarigama scaling at roughly 15 per Dive Weights cast (about 100 per cycle) was judged the safe upgrade. Pistol Sword's own active hit added about 800 he had not counted.
- Aquatics versus weapons: he plays safe lines on aquatics, aggressive high-roll lines on weapons.

#### Caveats or disagreements
- Calls the run unrepeatable: three top-tier skills early, then five days failing to find Pistol Sword.
- Unsure about Hellbilly over Bloodreef Raider (?), and about Blow Gun versus Pistol Sword at the end.
- Dislikes Berserker and Best Defense (?) skills; Trebuchet at silver judged too weak (gold or better needed).
- Finn's Big Bite versus Etherite (?) is untested since the new laser pistol.
- Weapons' skill dependence is the thing he likes least "right now".

### Checkable mechanics claims
- (V1) Burn ticks on a fixed half-second grid, so applying burn at 2.9 s yields a tick at 3.0 s that a 3.0 s application would miss.
- (V1) A merchant reroll costs 2 gold on day 1; at Kwixel (?) it costs 4.
- (V1) Selling Coral adds +10 to Coral Armor; Sea Shell also buffs it.
- (V1) Chum sells for its purchase price and leaves a Piranha.
- (V1) Lockbox: buy 6, +3 value per fight won.
- (V1) Primordial (?): charges 2 s when you burn, poison or freeze; per-trigger damage gain cut from 25 to 20 this patch (he later reads 25 on his own copy, possibly a higher tier).
- (V1) Dive Weights: multicast equals ammo; reduces cooldown of adjacent aquatic items; hastes an item per cast.
- (V1) A fiery-enchanted Iceberg yields two status procs per enemy item use.
- (V1) A "haste a burn item" start-of-fight skill cannot target Incendiary Rounds because it has no cooldown.
- (V1) Solar Farm with Rocket Boots has a 2 s cooldown.
- (V1) Arbalest works with a single ammo.
- (V1) Volcanic Vents 7 s cooldown; Lighter 3 s.
- (V2) Silver chocolate: +100 max health for 5 gold.
- (V2) Kyver Drone cannot win if the player fields no items.
- (V2) Dive Weights consumes one ammo per use, so its multicast drops by one each cycle.
- (V2) Shark Claws first fires at 6 s; its buff applied to a later-arriving weapon hit (he tested 60 doubling to 120).
- (V2) Crow's Nest gives 40% crit board-wide.
- (V2) Ammo-item loot is very likely to be a weapon.
- (V2) Curio's pool contains two slow buffs but haste buffs are rare (Rocket Boots).
- (V2) Pistol Sword triggers on every ammo use and also has its own active attack that can crit.
- (V2) "Kev" (?) merchant tends to offer Swash Buckle because he sells gold-tier items.

### 1. "I studied the rank 1 Vanessas for 1 week! This is what I learned!"

CurrentlyKevin | 23,555 views | uploaded 2025-07-02 | 863 s (14:23) | https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tJgit89IOQM

**Authority signals:** Small channel (680 followers) but the content is a study of three streamers who each hit rank 1 that season (Rahresh, FirstPinkBeaver, RagnarRegis), used with permission; the creator reports his own 10-win rate rising from about 35-40% to about 70% after one to two weeks of applying it.

**Core claims**
- Play for tempo: make the board as strong as possible every single day. Do not weaken today's board for a later payoff, and do not skip an item just because it is off-synergy; use it today and discard it tomorrow.
- Early wins matter most because every loss adds a day, and later days are more rock-paper-scissors (aggro beats scaling, sustain-to-sandstorm beats limited-damage aggro, scaling beats zero-pressure sustain). More days means more chances to meet a counter.
- In-combat tempo: trade raw power for speed. If the first item only fires at 5-6 seconds on day 6 or later, the board is probably too slow.
- The three rank-1 players do not share one playstyle. One hunts Langxian (?) with "metal and Ky drone" (unclear, possibly Metronome and another item); another almost never does; one favours slow/haste builds while two favour weapon builds. Better players succeed with a wider range of boards.
- Top players keep improving the board and look for pivots even while winning; they pivot when improvements stop coming or they feel behind for the day.
- Forcing a fixed build (his old habit) cost early fights. His progression: first aim to win all of days 1-5, then add mid/late planning on top.
- Practice method: pause a top player's VOD before each choice, decide yourself, then compare and work out the difference.

**Notable details**
- Holsters: the value is the build starting a few seconds earlier, even if nothing else on the board interacts with haste.
- Slow example: a gold Elemental Depth Charge with no cooldown reduction takes around 10 seconds; most opposing builds have finished by then.
- Toxic Flame build example: Dive Weights next to Incendiary Rounds would add five more Toxic Flame triggers, but his Weather Glass only begins at 7 seconds. He instead ran a diamond clam item (Clamera?) at 4 s plus a 3 s Lighter, with a skill captioned "Righty Tidy" (?) giving the clam 1 s of charge when the Lighter is used. In 3 seconds that gives three burn triggers for Zoarcid (?), cutting its 6 s cooldown to 3 s; it then grants 2 s of haste, so the payoff effectively lands at about 5 s.
- Freeze skills are valued for delaying the opponent's start, but your skills still need to trigger before their items do.
- Seven lookouts: (1) get a friend early; Tiny Furry Monster is high value and early skills win fights. (2) Plan for at least two shops on day 1. (3) Get Star Chart before day 4 to collect gold and XP at the docks on days 4-7. (4) Levels 4, 7, 10, 13 are power spikes; have the win condition before the level-7 one so it goes silver to gold (the caption says "day seven"). (5) "Old Zayn" (?) and "Vermeier" (?) can give Inexorable (?); "Professor Wrigle" (?) and "Malifang" (?) can give Toxic Flame. (6) Do not undervalue health: chocolate bars and +health events create breakpoints against monsters. (7) He nearly always takes Bazaaron (?) and Shrouded Figure for XP; for monsters, items/skills can outweigh XP.
- A vendor with nothing useful: 150 health from chocolates is still worth it.
- Decision examples: with Star Chart held, a top player still skipped Docks on day 5 to visit "Andy" (?) for Zoarcid, which is strong on Vanessa generally and especially with Trebuchet. On day 1 with a weak board, go to "JJ" (?) for items rather than "B1" (?) for a free bronze upgrade. Among skill vendors, a targeted freeze-skill vendor beat a gold-skill vendor because the gold pool is much larger. On day 3 with Tortuga and a strong board, take chocolates over "Quixle" (?); buy bronze or silver rather than gold to keep money, and bronze chocolates can be resold to "Vulpac" (?) for gold. At the level-7 choice (guaranteed silver upgrade or skills from "Argenta" (?)), skills were preferred because many outcomes help (Inexorable, Toxic Flame, crit, freeze, strength, +burn, Heated Shells) and the Trebuchet upgrade is modest. "Quixle" has roughly 100 items; standouts named: Zoarcid, Holsters, Shock Glasses (?), Powder Keg.
- His previous forced builds: early Shark Claws into a one-weapon late game; slow/haste Shrimp (?) with Tortuga, Depth Charge or Powder Keg; Trebuchet into Powder Keg.
- Tools: uses HowBazaar.gg and BazaarDB.gg to look up what any event, shop or monster can give.

**Caveats or disagreements**
- He states up front that specific picks may change with buffs, nerfs or expansions, so the video focuses on approach. A new season with new Vanessa items was days away.
- Pure early-win focus backfired at first: he spent all gold and often finished under 7 wins.
- Reading shops/events well takes experience; he says there is no shortcut.

### 2. "7 Tips For Playing Vanessa in The Bazaar"

Riveh | 2,745 views | uploaded 2025-07-28 | 193 s (3:13) | https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tqQ2jJ1N-1M

**Authority signals:** Small channel (379 followers); no rank claim in this video (his other video cites 250+ hours).

**Core claims**
- Jungle Ruins on day 1 or 2 hands out a guaranteed small silver weapon or apparel item from any hero, e.g. a silver Knee Brace or weapons Vanessa cannot normally get.
- Life Preserver (item name comes from the description; the caption skips it) acts like a free revive in the first few days and is best with poison, shields and heals, i.e. boards that want to stall.
- Always buy Star Chart in early shops: each Docks visit while it is in the inventory pays 5 gold plus 1 extra XP.
- An unnamed item (the description points to Wanted Poster) is described as a much better Star Chart that can snowball an XP lead into easy 10-win runs.
- Buy item generators early: Shovel first (gives other heroes' items), Fishing Rod second for aquatic builds, Piranha net (?) third.
- Bloodhound is called probably Vanessa's best skill, fitting nearly any build; take it on sight.
- Buy a bronze Cove early and leave it in the stash; it grows as you sell junk (chocolates, loot) and builds a gold reserve for pivots.

**Notable details**
- With Life Preserver, reaching sandstorm at equal HP is described as nearly always a win.
- The Docks option stops appearing after day 9, so sell Star Chart then.
- The poster-type item gives more total XP if it is on the board when you beat a ghost, but it adds little combat power; 2 XP from a win beats nothing from a loss. He has done this only once or twice.
- Enchanted generators produce items carrying the same enchantment.
- Island gives free HP or regen every hour, but starts at gold, so he says you will not see it about 90% of the time.
- Diamond skill "Reel Them In" (?) is the runner-up skill, rare and late-game only.

**Caveats or disagreements**
- Putting the XP item on the board is flagged as at-your-own-risk.
- No patch hedging stated; the video dates from July 2025.

### 3. "10 Ways To Improve Your Runs In The Bazaar!"

Riveh | 4,780 views | uploaded 2025-07-20 | 973 s (16:13) | https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tISFeoWXsWo

**Authority signals:** Self-described as not a pro; 250+ hours, shows a trophy breakdown, has mentored two friends; aimed at players stuck at 2-3 wins.

**Core claims**
- Starting pick: economy is the safe option, gold skill is fun but risky (no money, and e.g. +40 damage is wasted if no weapon turns up), enchanted item is his preferred middle ground.
- Shops are the default choice whenever the build is not finished; early on, a full board of filler beats one buffed silver item.
- Do not skip HP: the 5-gold chocolate option gives exactly 100 HP and can decide day 2-3 fights.
- XP is king: he takes XP roughly nine times in ten. A one-level lead is strong; two or more is overwhelming.
- Hold, do not sell: keep a full stash for flexibility and for merchants who pay extra.
- Boosts are underrated once the build is good; the goal is 10 wins, so raising the odds of the current fight is the point.
- Early wins predict the run: one win by day 5-6 usually means trouble.

**Notable details**
- Reroll rules: always reroll at 2-gold shops whose pool you want; almost never pay 4 gold to roll in the first 3-4 days. Generic vendors (small, medium, weapon, non-weapon, "JJ" (?)) roll for 2; specialised vendors cost 4 up to 8 depending on rarity and pool.
- Stash items count as net worth, so zero gold does not always mean you cannot shop.
- A bad enchanted-item start can be salvaged: keep a good enchant (icy, shiny) and transform the item later via the vendor or Mak's catalysts.
- HP sources: chocolate contest (needs inventory space); Knee Brace hunting at Curio (riskier, 4-gold rolls); Snack Time (free, no space; worth it past 100 HP unless the alternative is far better); Finn's Big Bite (?) on day 1 for 5 regen, still good on days 2-3. He notes 400-500 HP can decide early fights.
- Auto-pick ranking: (1) free enchants, which can double to quadruple an item; (2) free loot, where feathers are his best loot and XP vials the fallback; (3) Pearl's Dig Site for off-hero items; (4) "Hattie" (?), sometimes a free gold skill, otherwise gold; (5) tie between Thieves Guild, Bounty Agents (?), Deadly Monster, Bazaaron (?), Shrouded Figure, all for XP.
- Level-ups give skills, more HP, extra board slots for the first three levels, and a free enchant at level 10.
- Use the post-fight recap to find the carry (e.g. one item at 4,000 damage versus others at 400-500).
- Sell only to fund a purchase, to free space, or when you own a daily generator of gold/consumables. "Barkin" (Barkun?) buys chocolates back at 1 gold each; "Midun" (?) pays 2 extra gold for medium items. Proboscis is his example of a keep-in-stash item for slow builds. Leave slots free for daily generators.
- Boosting: at Jules's Cafe always take the HP upgrade. Weigh shop odds against the boost, e.g. a large-item shop when you own only one large item. One or two wins from 10, a random item hunt adds little.
- For day 1-2 wins: buy 2-gold filler, grab a Catfish for poison, take regen items.

**Caveats or disagreements**
- Says there is rarely a single optimal play and repeatedly notes exceptions.
- Not every hero can win early; Pygmalien is his example.
- Treat anything beyond a silver result as a win and judge skill over 10-100 runs; strong 9-win runs still lose to extreme boards (a 30,000 HP Pyg, a Mak with diamond lifesteal Femur plus eight slow items).
- Reroll prices here differ from his 2026 video (see section 4).

### 4. "Ten Tips for Beginners in the Bazaar!"

Riveh | 5,779 views | uploaded 2026-06-01 | 471 s (7:51) | https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Q6dtyjWCvT8

**Authority signals:** Same small channel; beginner-oriented, no rank claim made in the video.

**Core claims**
- Never lose the guaranteed monster fights, especially on days 1-6; if unsure of the board, fight the bronze monster, which he calls nearly impossible to lose.
- XP is the most important stat; take it wherever offered. Named XP sources: random encounter, Mountain Pass, Study, plus options unlocked by certain stash items.
- Keep the stash full (10 slots): hold strong items that do not fit yet, daily generators, and items to sell at specific shops for more.
- Shop more the weaker the board is and less the stronger it is; never enter a shop with no gold.
- Fill the board in the first few days, even with filler, because early wins are within your control while anything after day 10 is a coin flip between extreme builds.
- Find the carry, then ask how to support it. Example: Jaballian War Drums (?) supported by as many small, fast weapons as possible.
- Transmute off-build enchanted items instead of selling them.

**Notable details**
- Reroll cost is shown by the merchant's border: bronze 2, silver 3, gold 4, diamond 6. Check it before entering.
- Level leads give extra item slots early, a free enchant at level 10, and diamond skills late. He shows an early fight with a 1,300 HP advantage.
- Items generated at the start of a day are lost without warning if the stash has no room.
- Auto-picks besides extra monster fights: free enchants (shield, doubled damage, shiny); Monster Ranch (?) for feathers (cooldown reduction) or XP vials; Pearl's Dig Site, his top pick, since the item is free and can be sold if unusable, but do not burn all gold rerolling there; "Haddie" (?); expeditions or expedition tickets for lots of gold and sometimes items or enchants. Between the day-6 and day-9 expedition he prefers day 6 as more consistent.

### 1. How Do Haste and Charge Work? | The Bazaar

**Header:** "How Do Haste and Charge Work? | The Bazaar" | Momo vs Spire (132 followers) | 3,789 views | uploaded 2024-11-04 | 198 s (3:18) | https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=J6T0_a1SZOM

**Authority signals:** Tiny channel, no rank claimed; a short explainer narrated over the creator's own Vanessa aquatic board. The description says the mechanics confused the creator at first.

**Core claims (every rule the video states):**
- Cooldown basics: an item's cooldown is printed under its name. The timer starts when the fight starts; the item is used when the timer completes, then the timer restarts and repeats. Example: Jellyfish with an 8 s cooldown fires at 8 s, again 8 s later, and so on.
- Haste: a hasted item moves through its cooldown twice as fast. 1 second of haste gets through 2 seconds of cooldown during that second.
- Worked example: 4 seconds of haste on the 8 s Jellyfish is enough to complete one full cooldown.
- Haste durations add up: Jellyfish gains 1 s of haste each time another aquatic item is used, and a neighbouring Fishing Rod also hasted it, so it showed more than 1 s. The creator says it sometimes "stacks up" a few seconds of haste, and for that whole period it cools down at double speed.
- Charge: charging an item by N seconds takes a flat N seconds off the time remaining until its next use. It does not change the item's cooldown value itself; only the current cycle is advanced.
- Worked example: Dam starts at a 25 s cooldown; each use of another aquatic item pushes its timer forward 2 s.
- Multicast: an item with multicast N is used N times when it triggers (multicast 3 = three uses). Each of those uses counts separately as a trigger, so each one charges Dam by 2 s.
- No cap: the creator says charge "effectively" has no limit on how fast cooldowns can cycle; with enough charge sources an item can fire again and again in rapid succession. Calls charge extremely potent for this reason.

**Notable details:**
- UI (video and description): the green number near the top of an item is its remaining haste duration; the red number near the bottom is its remaining slow duration.
- Board shown: Jellyfish, Fishing Rod, Dam, other small aquatic items, most of them with multicast. Why it works: every aquatic use both hastes Jellyfish (+1 s) and charges Dam (+2 s), and multicast multiplies the number of uses.
- No hero, day, merchant or economy advice in this video.

**Caveats or disagreements:**
- Freeze: the creator is only "pretty sure" that a frozen item can still be used if its cooldown is charged all the way to completion, and says outright there is no video proof. Treat as unverified.
- Slow: the video states NO rule for slow. The only mention is the red-number UI note in the description. Nothing about slow halving speed, or about haste and slow cancelling.
- Nothing is said about what happens to excess charge beyond the remaining time, about whether haste durations refresh versus add (the wording implies add), or about any minimum cooldown.
- Description: the item numbers are from an early build and may be rebalanced; the creator expects haste and charge themselves not to change. Specific values (Jellyfish 8 s, Dam 25 s and +2 s per aquatic use, Jellyfish +1 s haste) are Nov 2024 closed-beta numbers and are likely outdated.

- Tip 3, level-up rewards: usually take the middle option (gold plus a loot item). Exceptions: level 4 upgrades a Bronze item to Silver (have a Bronze item worth upgrading by then, or plan on the Bronze skill); level 7 upgrades Silver to Gold; level 10 gives an enchantment; level 13 upgrades an item of any tier.

### Checkable mechanics claims

From video 1 (J6T0_a1SZOM), haste and charge:
1. Cooldown timers start at fight start; an item fires each time its timer completes, then the timer restarts.
2. Haste makes an item progress its cooldown at exactly 2x rate (1 s of haste = 2 s of cooldown progress).
3. 4 s of haste completes one full cycle of an 8 s cooldown item.
4. Haste durations from separate sources or triggers add together on one item (shown as a green number at the top of the item).
5. Slow duration is shown as a red number near the bottom of the item (the video gives no slow rate).
6. Charge N removes a flat N seconds from the time remaining to the item's next use; it does not alter the item's base cooldown.
7. Each individual use from a multicast item counts as a separate "item used" trigger (multicast 3 = 3 triggers, so 3 charges on Dam).
8. Charge has no cap on how quickly an item can re-fire.
9. UNVERIFIED by the creator: a frozen item that is charged to full cooldown completion still gets used.
10. Item values at the time (Nov 2024): Jellyfish 8 s cooldown, +1 s haste when another aquatic item is used; Dam 25 s cooldown, charged 2 s per other aquatic item used; Fishing Rod hastes an adjacent item.

## Synthesis

### Consensus
- **Win the early days.** Make today's board as strong as possible, fill the board even with filler, and do not skip an item because it is off-synergy (CurrentlyKevin; Riveh "10 ways"; Riveh "beginners"; Treb). A loss adds a day, and later days are more rock-paper-scissors.
- **Experience is the most valuable stat.** Take XP wherever offered; levels 4, 7, 10 and 13 are the power spikes (CurrentlyKevin; Riveh, both videos; Volf; Treb).
- **Health is cheap and decides early fights.** The 5-gold chocolate option is worth it; Volf aims for about 200 bonus max health on Vanessa (Riveh; CurrentlyKevin; Volf).
- **Keep the stash full; sell only for a reason** (space, a purchase, a merchant who pays extra) (Riveh, both videos; Volf's hedge-in-the-stash habit).
- **Find the carry, then support it** (Riveh; Volf: many fast triggers, then multiply them, then add speed).
- **Speed inside the fight matters.** If the first item fires at 5-6 seconds on day 6 or later the board is too slow (CurrentlyKevin; Volf's "eight seconds and you're dead").
- **Do not chase an item before its odds are real.** Gold-tier items first appear on day 6 with tiny odds (Game Plan HQ); strengthen the current board until then.

### Contested / split
- **Reroll costs.** Riveh 2025: 2 gold at generic vendors, 4-8 at specialised ones. Riveh 2026: by merchant border, bronze 2 / silver 3 / gold 4 / diamond 6. The game data (below) matches neither exactly.
- **Starting pick.** Riveh prefers the enchanted item, calls economy safe and a gold skill risky; Volf says not to take economy on day 1 and takes a skill.
- **Forcing a build.** CurrentlyKevin argues against it; Volf's weapons guide is a deliberate forced line, and he calls the run a high roll.
- **Shields.** Volf's aquatic line leans on cheap early shield (Coral Armor); his weapons line calls extra shield a dilution and uses max health as the only defence.
- **Jungle Ruins.** Riveh: a guaranteed small silver weapon or apparel item; CurrentlyKevin and Volf: burn, crit or gold outcomes.

### Gaps for guide coverage
- No captions for the three newest Vanessa guides (Volf, November 2026), so the current patch's creator view is missing.
- Nothing usable on positioning beyond single examples; the game data's adjacency rules are the better source.
- Board size by level (6 slots early, 8 at level 3 per Treb) is not confirmed in the data and is not used by the app yet.
- No creator covers how monsters should be chosen in numbers; advice is anecdotal.

### Recency & meta shift notes
- Six of the twelve videos are from 2024 or 2025. Item-specific advice from them is unreliable: four of the item claims checked above no longer match the data.
- The tier list (November 2024) predates open ranked play and new heroes and should be ignored.
- General principles (tempo, XP, health, full stash) are repeated across 2025 and 2026 videos and are the durable part.

### Creator-specific biases
- **Volf** plays for high rolls on weapons and safe lines on aquatics, by his own description; both recorded runs were unusually lucky.
- **CurrentlyKevin** reports other players' habits, not his own results at that rank.
- **Riveh** writes for players stuck at low win counts; advice favours safety and consistency.
- **Momo vs Spire**'s content is from the closed beta.

### How the companion uses this
- Four principles are shown in the panel as "Görüş" with the creator named: fill the board in the first five days, a first item slower than about five seconds from day 6, do not hunt gold-tier items early (with the day's real odds from the data), keep the stash full.
- The engine now counts each cast of a multicast item as its own use.
- Nothing else from the videos changes a number: item values come from the game data.

## Raw data
Transcripts + metadata saved to: `data/research/yt-raw-2026-11-23-a.json` and `data/research/yt-raw-2026-11-23-b.json` (local, not committed).
